entry.title: [ahmadzeidabad] Negotiation as a tactic of war or a tool in the service of peace?…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @ahmadzeidabad

Negotiation as a tactic of war or a tool in the service of peace? Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf, the Speaker of the Parliament, has repeated for the umpteenth time that "we fight and we negotiate." Yes. There is no contradiction between war and negotiation such that one must choose one or the other. But what is meant by negotiation? Is negotiation a tool for achieving peace and ending hostility? Or is it a tactic to create opportunities and buy time to equip oneself in order to be better prepared to continue the war? If the second meaning is intended, then framing the war-negotiation duality is pointless, because in that case negotiation amounts to nothing more than a tactic of war. But if what is meant by negotiation is ending the war and achieving peace, then the war-peace duality is a more logical substitute for the war-negotiation duality. War and peace, however, unlike war and negotiation, are contradictory and cannot be reconciled; therefore, one must inevitably choose between them. In my view, our country has now reached a point where it must inevitably choose between war and peace. Mr. Qalibaf, as the head of Iran's negotiating team, is obliged to confront public opinion on this matter with greater candor and courage. It is the responsibility of Mr. Qalibaf and other officials who speak on this matter to give these terms conceptual clarity. Words and expressions without conceptual clarity are like balloons full of air and serve more for entertainment than for conveying a message and clarifying a goal! The political atmosphere of our country has become so bloated from the sheer volume and accumulation of undefined words that everyone is bewildered and dazed! #احمد_زیدآبادی @ahmadzeidabad
